items_missed: Never asked "How are you today?" after greeting the customer
No explicit agenda statement (what he'd cover, how long it'd take) or a 'sound good?' confirmation before diving in
Didn't probe special considerations like narrow hallways, tight turns, or long carry distances
Didn't ask about packing needs or how many boxes are at the apartment (only got 'no boxes' for the storage unit, unprompted)
Never asked a moving-stressors question (e.g. 'anything you're particularly worried about?')
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000 protection) was never mentioned
Meet Your Mover program (photo/info email before the move) was never mentioned
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after explaining the 2.5-hr minimum / 15-min proration
Walk distance, traffic, and time-equivalent comparisons (e.g. school-bus reference) weren't used to justify the 5.5-hr estimate
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped — no consolidation tips (loose items, drawers) and no 'take a carload yourself' tip
No email confirmation/handoff mentioned even though the customer was told to 'call back to confirm' — no bolded detail summary, no 'reply with corrections' ask
Never proactively asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the customer had to prompt that topic herself
Never stated business hours or how to reach Einstein Moving to lock in the booking
Never used the customer's name (Austen) once in the entire 12.7-minute call, even though she used his name twice
No explicit insurance/No Worries explanation, and FAQs (hourly billing, gas fees) were answered reactively only after the customer asked rather than being addressed proactively
top_strength: Jack gave a clear, specific, itemized time and price estimate (5.5 hours, $1,199 — apartment time plus storage add plus buffer) and made a real same-call booking push by flagging that only one Saturday slot was left.
coaching_note: Jack skipped the entire Save Your Ass prep speech and all three key differentiators (No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee), and never used the customer's name once — weaving those into the pricing walkthrough would likely have reduced the 'let me check other quotes' hesitation at the close.
phone_presence_notes: Friendly, casual tone throughout ('cool,' 'no worries,' 'perfect') and the call stayed pleasant, but it was transactional — no use of the customer's name and no acknowledgment of her explicit hesitation about checking other quotes.
audio_review_reason: Transcript has several garbled/mistranscribed segments (e.g. 'fifth flori. To El eleventh', 'on the Grali all the units') that limit confidence in the phone-presence read from text alone.
